h1: Socorro Municipal Court Traffic Ticket Lawyer
intro: Socorro police write more traffic tickets per mile of road than almost any department in the county, and every one of them lands in Socorro Municipal Court. For a flat $69, attorney Robert Navar appears there for you and works to keep the ticket off your record.
summary: Socorro Municipal Court hears Class C citations written by the Socorro Police Department, which patrols North Loop Dr, Alameda Ave and Socorro Rd aggressively for speed, insurance and registration violations.
Our flat fee for Socorro Municipal Court is $69 per citation, with discounted add-ons for extra tickets from the same stop. Hire online or call 915-503-1600.
We file the appearance, attend the docket and negotiate with the city prosecutor — most Socorro clients never appear in court.
Results we work for: dismissal, deferred disposition under art. 45.051, a defensive-driving dismissal, or a non-moving reduction when deferral is not offered.
Lower Valley tickets from Sheriff's deputies, DPS troopers or constables go to a county JP court, not Socorro — check the agency on your citation.

sections.heading: Why So Many Lower Valley Drivers Get Socorro Tickets
paragraphs: Socorro sits between El Paso and San Elizario in the Lower Valley, and three of the valley's main roads run straight through it: North Loop Dr, Alameda Ave (Highway 20) and Socorro Rd. Thousands of drivers who live in El Paso, Horizon City, Clint and San Elizario pass through Socorro every day on the way to work, and the Socorro Police Department has a long-standing reputation for working those corridors hard. Speed enforcement on North Loop and Alameda, insurance and registration stops, and school-zone enforcement near the Socorro ISD campuses produce a steady stream of citations.

All of those tickets are filed in Socorro Municipal Court, which is the City of Socorro's own court with its own judge, clerk and prosecutor. If the officer was a Sheriff's deputy, a DPS trooper or a constable on the same stretch of Alameda, the case goes to an El Paso County Justice of the Peace precinct instead, and a ticket from El Paso police on the city side of the line goes to El Paso Municipal Court. The issuing agency printed on the citation decides; our free ticket and warrant lookup can confirm it.

sections.heading: What Socorro Police Typically Cite
paragraphs: The mix of Socorro tickets we see at our office is heavy on speeding — often on North Loop where the posted limit drops as the road passes through neighborhoods — and on compliance charges. Failure to maintain financial responsibility under Transportation Code 601.191 carries a $175–$350 fine for a first offense and is one of the most common Socorro citations. Expired registration, no driver's license and driving while license invalid round out the list.

Compliance charges are also where a lawyer gets the fastest results. Socorro's prosecutor will typically dismiss a no-insurance or registration ticket when we show the problem was fixed, so the first thing we ask new clients is to bring their current insurance card and registration. Stops that produce two or three citations at once are common on Alameda, and we handle each additional ticket at a discounted add-on rate rather than a second full fee.

Socorro's enforcement reputation cuts both ways in court. Officers who write high volumes of tickets make mistakes on citations, and the same officer may have dozens of cases on a single docket. A defect in the citation, or an officer who cannot attend a trial setting, is leverage we use for a dismissal.

sections.heading: How Socorro Municipal Court Handles a Ticket
paragraphs: Socorro Municipal Court holds traffic dockets on a limited schedule rather than daily, so a driver who misses the appearance date or shows up on a non-docket day can wait weeks for the next setting. Verify the current docket schedule with the court before going yourself. When you hire us, we file a notice of appearance and a not-guilty plea before your date, and the court sets the case for pretrial. Robert Navar or a member of our staff attends, confers with the city prosecutor and negotiates; you stay at work.

Like every Class C court in Texas, Socorro can grant deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45.051 — a special expense fee, a 90–180 day violation-free period, and a dismissal with no conviction — and a driving safety course dismissal under art. 45.0511 for eligible drivers. Eligibility rules, costs and the reasons a court might refuse are on our deferred adjudication and defensive driving page. For drivers cited 25 mph or more over, CDL holders and repeat cases, we negotiate for deferral or a non-moving reduction instead.

sections.heading: Our $69 Flat Fee for Socorro Municipal Court
paragraphs: We charge $69 per citation in Socorro Municipal Court. That covers the appearance, every docket setting and the closing paperwork. Court fees for a deferral or course are paid to the court separately. Additional citations from the same stop — speeding plus no insurance, for example — are $10–$30 add-ons at checkout. Socorro warrants are $35 for the first and $20 for each additional and are handled with the ticket.

A paid ticket is a conviction. A speeding conviction adds two points and three years of higher premiums; a no-insurance conviction can cost more, because some carriers treat it as a reason to drop or surcharge the policy. The $69 fee that in most cases ends in a dismissal is the cheaper path. The consultation is free, and se habla español — many of our Socorro clients prefer to handle their case in Spanish.

sections.heading: Socorro Warrants and Old Tickets
paragraphs: Because Socorro writes so many tickets to drivers who do not live there, forgotten Socorro citations are common. A missed appearance date produces a warrant and a separate failure-to-appear charge, and the city reports unresolved cases to the state's Failure to Appear program, which places an OMNI hold on your license renewal. Many clients first learn about an old Socorro ticket when DPS refuses to renew their license.

We file the appearance, request the warrant recall and ask the court to reset the ticket on its next docket, as described on the traffic warrant recall and OMNI hold removal pages. Once the hold clears, you can renew at DPS while the underlying ticket is resolved.

sections.heading: What to Do After a Socorro Ticket
paragraphs: Check the appearance date, do not pay the ticket and do not request defensive driving yourself. Fix any compliance problem now — renew the registration, get the insurance card — and send us the citation through the online form or call 915-503-1600. We confirm the court, the fee and the plan the same day.
This page is general information, not legal advice about your case. Verify the current docket schedule with Socorro Municipal Court, or let our office confirm it for you.

faqs.q: Which tickets go to Socorro Municipal Court?
faqs.a: Citations written by the Socorro Police Department inside the city limits, including North Loop Dr, Alameda Ave and Socorro Rd. Tickets from Sheriff's deputies, DPS troopers or constables in the same area go to an El Paso County JP precinct.

faqs.q: How much does a lawyer cost for a Socorro ticket?
faqs.a: A flat $69 per citation. Extra citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons, and warrants are $35 for the first and $20 for each additional one.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to Socorro Municipal Court myself?
faqs.a: Usually not. We file the appearance and attend the docket for you. A personal appearance is only needed if the case goes to trial, which is rare and something we would discuss with you first.

faqs.q: Socorro gave me a no-insurance ticket but I actually had insurance. Can it be dismissed?
faqs.a: Often, yes. If you had a valid policy on the date of the stop, we present the proof to the prosecutor and ask for a dismissal. If you got insurance afterward, courts frequently dismiss on compliance as well — see our no insurance ticket page.

faqs.q: I don't live in Socorro and forgot about the ticket. What happens?
faqs.a: There is likely a warrant and an OMNI hold that blocks your license renewal. Call us the same day; we file the appearance, request the recall and get the ticket back on a docket — see traffic warrant recall.

faqs.q: Will Socorro Municipal Court give me deferred disposition?
faqs.a: For most ordinary moving violations, yes. High-speed, CDL and repeat cases are handled more strictly, which is where an attorney's request carries more weight than a driver's.
